profile.name: search
profile.purpose: Reduced GA development budget; disjoint from final reporting seeds

native_metadata.patch_description: Reduce sigma to 0.15 to make smaller mutations that may preserve successful CartPole policies. Reduce elite_ratio to 0.20 to concentrate reproduction on higher-performing candidates. This balances local exploration with stronger selection; improvement remains to be measured with the search profile.

Try sigma 0.10 and elite_ratio 0.15. The search results favor smaller mutations and a lower elite ratio than the original configuration. This proposal extends that direction moderately: smaller mutations may preserve successful balancing policies, while fewer elites increase selection pressure. Improvement remains to be verified with the search profile.

Search results favor lower mutation strength and elite ratio. Try sigma 0.07 and elite_ratio 0.10 to refine successful policies with smaller perturbations and concentrate selection on stronger performers. This extrapolates from the best observed configuration; improvement remains to be verified using the search profile.

The search results improve as sigma and elite_ratio decrease. Propose sigma 0.05 and elite_ratio 0.08 to test a modest continuation of this trend: smaller mutations may preserve successful policies, while a smaller elite fraction concentrates selection on stronger candidates. This configuration requires search-profile evaluation to confirm improvement.

The best observed configuration uses sigma 0.07 and elite_ratio 0.10. Propose a nearby setting of 0.075 and 0.11 to modestly increase exploration and elite retention while staying close to that successful region. This is an untested candidate for the search profile.

The search results favor smaller mutations and stronger selection. This proposal extends that trend with sigma 0.05 and elite_ratio 0.075, aiming for finer policy refinement while retaining mutation-driven exploration. It changes only the static configuration; improved performance remains to be verified with the search profile.

The search results improve as sigma and elite_ratio decrease. Propose sigma 0.035 and elite_ratio 0.05 to test whether smaller mutations and stronger selection further improve performance. Smaller mutations may preserve effective policies while still supporting adaptation. This configuration needs evaluation with the search profile; improvement is not yet verified.

The GA’s tunable parameters are mutation scale (`sigma`) and elite selection fraction (`elite_ratio`). The best observed configuration used 0.05 and 0.075. This proposal tests a nearby setting: slightly smaller mutations for finer refinement and slightly more elites to preserve successful policies during continual learning. Improvement requires validation with the search profile.

Keep the fixed GA and its best observed elite ratio, while reducing sigma to 0.045 for finer policy adjustments. This configuration may improve refinement while retaining exploration; improved performance requires search-profile evaluation.

Propose sigma 0.055 and elite_ratio 0.075. Search results favor increasing sigma from 0.045 to 0.05 and reducing elite_ratio from 0.085 to 0.075. This candidate retains the better observed elite ratio while testing a modest further increase in mutation strength to improve exploration. Its performance remains to be measured with the search profile.

Test sigma 0.065 with elite_ratio 0.075. Both prior configurations improved on the current settings, and 0.055 marginally outperformed 0.05. A modest further increase in mutation scale may improve exploration during continual adaptation while retaining the better-performing elite ratio. This is an untested proposal for the search profile.

Increase sigma to 0.08 while keeping elite_ratio at 0.075. The search results favor 0.065 over 0.05 and 0.055, suggesting that stronger mutation may improve exploration as CartPole conditions change. This proposal tests a modest further increase while isolating its effect; improved performance remains to be verified with the search profile.

comparison.interpretation: Development configuration search only. Repeated duplicate and partial failed evaluations remain charged as actual work. No held-out performance or search-method superiority is established.

model_usage.interpretation: CLI launches and stored response usage are observed. Internal provider requests, quota remaining, and account billing are not observable here. Headless default-zero reasoning/tool fields are treated as unavailable. Headless's Codex input count excludes cached input; Shinka does not retain the cached count, so total prompt tokens are unavailable. Native price estimates are not subscription charges.

artifact_policy: Raw text and a readable SQLite snapshot are exported with local root paths redacted. Binary checkpoints and native SQLite remain local with hashes. Model-equivalent prices are not subscription charges.
